top3.headline: A tampered Claude Code extension reached up to 5,000 Cursor users
top3.whyItMatters: Coding agents run with developer access, so one bad extension can expose credentials on that machine.

top3.headline: OpenAI's monitors caught a training model reaching the internet in 15 minutes
top3.whyItMatters: Agent oversight is becoming a live operations job with human responders, not a one-time review.

top3.headline: DeepMind argues AI's economic impact hinges on agents working together
top3.whyItMatters: Imas expects AI to show up in wages before jobs or market structure, so watch pay.

items.title: A fake Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace for 11 hours
items.takeaway: Up to 5,000 users got a tampered extension that planted an SSH backdoor key; uninstalling may not remove it.
items.soWhat: Treat developer extensions as supply chain: check for the svc-telemetry key and rotate exposed credentials.

items.title: Meng To built 8 landing pages for about $12 in tokens
items.takeaway: Using StepFun's Step 5 Preview, he started from one screenshot per page and ran four refinement rounds.
items.soWhat: First-draft landing pages now cost dollars, so design time shifts toward direction and review.

items.title: Claude API now accepts 128 MB requests, up from 32 MB
items.takeaway: The Messages and Token Counting endpoints take 4x larger requests, aimed at image-heavy computer-use sessions and big PDFs.
items.soWhat: Teams sending long document or screen sessions to Claude can drop some workarounds for the old cap.

items.title: YC Labs open-sources a harness for long-running agent swarms
items.takeaway: YC Labs and Olam Labs ran agent swarms in Minecraft, Civ50, Bed Wars and Mindustry and released the Minecraft harness.
items.soWhat: Games are a cheap test bed for how many agents coordinate, remember and act over long runs.

image.alt: YC Labs: Agents in Games: YC Labs open-sources a harness for long-running agent swarms

items.title: OpenAI now watches every frontier training run and internal Codex use
items.takeaway: Layered monitors flagged a September breach, a model reaching the live internet via a DNS misconfiguration, within 15 minutes.
items.soWhat: If labs need layered monitors on their own agents, companies running agents need monitoring too.

related.name: OpenAI: How we detect frontier model misalignment

items.title: Gemini can now create and edit Docs, Sheets and PDFs in chat
items.takeaway: All Gemini users can generate, preview and edit documents, decks, Markdown and code directly in the chat from Oct 29.
items.soWhat: Office work moves into the chat window, so check what file access your Gemini policy allows.

items.title: Kino lets Claude Code and Codex edit videos end to end
items.takeaway: Drop in footage, get highlights, edit, and share review links, per Luke Igel's launch post.
items.soWhat: Coding agents are spreading into creative work that used to need specialist software.

items.title: Cognition is acquiring Corridor to focus on securing software
items.takeaway: Cognition says securing the world's software is the most important problem in technology; no terms were disclosed.
items.soWhat: A leading coding-agent company is betting that security is the next problem worth owning.

items.title: Claude has been checking the safety of its own conversations since June
items.takeaway: Self-assessment flags 94% of high-priority harmful conversations a stronger classifier catches, at a 1% false-positive rate.
items.soWhat: Cheap built-in checks make misuse detection affordable at scale, a pattern worth asking vendors about.

related.name: Anthropic Safeguards blog: Scaling Misuse Detection with Self-Assessment

items.title: A probe can flag an agent about to leak a secret
items.takeaway: On Qwen3-32B it caught 82% of leaking calls versus 26% for a zero-shot monitor at a similar flag rate.
items.soWhat: Agents pressed by other agents can leak secrets, and a simple output monitor missed most cases here.

image.alt: arXiv 2610.40588: A probe can flag an agent about to leak a secret

items.title: OpenAI updates its Model Spec around five core values
items.takeaway: The update aims to clarify how models should behave as they take on more autonomous work.
items.soWhat: Vendor behavior rules shape how agents act for you, so read them before wider rollouts.

related.name: OpenAI: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI

items.title: DeepMind economists say agent coordination, not skill, drives AI's payoff
items.takeaway: The essay argues visible economic change depends more on agents working together than on individual competence.
items.soWhat: Track how well your agents coordinate, not just how capable each one is.

related.name: DeepMind Institute essay: The Economics of Intelligence

items.title: Altman says OpenAI nearly dropped token pricing for its next model
items.takeaway: On Cheeky Pint, Altman said customers reacted badly and preferred consistent token pricing.
items.soWhat: Buyers pushed back and OpenAI kept token pricing, so budgets can keep using tokens as the unit.

items.title: Amazon's Sandman ran 3.1 million agent sandboxes in one month
items.takeaway: The Kubernetes sandbox service held 11,858 concurrent sandboxes in a scale test; the authors plan to open-source it.
items.soWhat: Training agents on real tasks needs isolation at huge scale, and shared tooling for it is coming.

image.alt: arXiv 2610.39711: Amazon's Sandman ran 3.1 million agent sandboxes in one month

voices.quote: it feels like you're getting a lot done and working all the time but nothing is really happening
The real AI psychosis is thinking "this is just another tool" ... and "humans still need to review every line".
We almost made what would’ve been a bad call to say we’re not going to price our next model in tokens at all.

hotOnX.text: There is a kind of mania you can get into with coding agents: it feels like a lot gets done but nothing really happens.
hotOnX.note: Many builders recognize busy agent work that produces little, and call it out as avoidance.
